title: Pre-Analysis — Blocker Door Link Bushing Standard Against the Inspection Bridge
abstract: Closed work order examining how long the wear inspection bulletin has to remain in force alongside the bushing modification, delegated to the maintenance programme owner.

sections.objective: Establish how long the blocker door link wear inspection has to remain in force alongside the self-lubricating bushing modification, given that the modification can only be embodied at reverser overhaul and the fleet overhaul interval is longer than the inspection interval by a factor of four.
sections.findings_summary: The inspection has to remain in force for considerably longer than the bulletin implies. The modification is a shop task and the shop visit is driven by the reverser overhaul interval, so a large part of the fleet will carry the pre-modification bushing for another eight to ten years. The inspection bulletin is written as a bridge and its compliance time reads as though the modification were an on-wing option, which it is not. The deployment timing comparison in the installation task is the other route to finding a worn link, and it is arguably better than the bore gauge because it needs no disassembly, but it depends on a previous record existing for the same engine and many operators do not keep one. That is a maintenance programme question rather than a design one. Nothing about the modification itself needed changing.
sections.next_steps: Delegate the inspection duration to the maintenance programme owner with the overhaul interval data attached. Recommend that the deployment timing comparison be made a recorded item so that the trend exists. Leave the modification and the bulletins as written.

similarity_seeds: blocker door link bushing worn oval on the loaded flank
reverser deployment times drifting apart between halves

tasks.title: Extract the fleet reverser overhaul interval distribution
Assess the deployment timing comparison as an alternative
Establish who owns the inspection duration decision

evidence.similarity_note: Found through the compliance time in the inspection bulletin, which assumes an embodiment opportunity that the modification route does not provide.

expected_findings.rationale: The inspection bulletin reads as a short bridge to the modification. Because the modification is a shop task on an overhaul-driven interval, the bridge is eight to ten years long for much of the fleet and the compliance wording does not reflect that.
expected_findings.resolution: Restate the inspection duration against the overhaul interval rather than against the modification availability.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the seal and clevis pin part numbers the task calls out.

expected_findings.rationale: The deployment timing comparison in the installation task is the only wear indication that needs no disassembly, and it depends on a previous record for the same engine. The task asks for the comparison but does not require the record to be kept.
expected_findings.resolution: Make the timing record a required entry rather than a recommendation.

evidence.similarity_note: Surfaced by similarity alone; the crew entry and the modification share no identifier and describe deployment from entirely different points of view.

expected_findings.rationale: The performance entry already asks crews to report a reverser that deploys slowly or asymmetrically even where nothing is annunciated. That report is the earliest available indication of link wear and nothing connects it to the maintenance action.
expected_findings.resolution: Route crew reports of slow or asymmetric deployment to the link inspection rather than to a general reverser defect.

type_data.conclusion: Closed and delegated. The inspection has to run far longer than the bulletin implies.
